quote: my wife had had some medical challenges.
stewart_read: This is the customer's actual interest reason and a vulnerability disclosure combined — the rep files it and pivots to the roof pitch instead of acknowledging it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically avoiding dwelling on a sensitive topic to keep the call moving efficiently, but there's no acknowledgment at all, not even a brief one, so reactive omission is more supported.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ("that's a big reason people look into this — sorry to hear that") costs nothing and builds trust before the harder qualifier questions.

quote: my wife has just recently stopped working because of her stroke.
stewart_read: Second disclosure of the same vulnerability theme, again unacknowledged; rep moves straight back to the taxable-income yes/no test.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be trying to stay in scope and not overstep into personal territory, but silence here reads as procedural tunnel vision rather than deliberate restraint.
coaching_implication: Bridge briefly then continue the qualifier — empathy and script progress are not mutually exclusive.

quote: my wife's physical conditions. I have to limit things anyway.
stewart_read: Third and final touch on the same vulnerability, now directly blocking the appointment timing; rep's response is generic agreement with no bridge to flexibility or urgency.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to offer a low-commitment, flexible next step (e.g., a phone-only design review) tailored to the caregiving constraint, not just accept the delay.

quote: if I made that request, it either bounced around there or some time ago. Maybe I'm demented, but that's fine.
stewart_read: Customer immediately questions the premise of the call; rep's intro never re-establishes concrete lead legitimacy (no specific ad/date reference) until several lines later.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep does eventually reference the date of the request at 01:34 ("it was last month on the eleventh"), so this is a delayed recovery rather than a total omission.
coaching_implication: Front-load the specific lead-source detail (date/channel) in the first exchange to defuse the "did I even request this" doubt immediately.

quote: It's yeah. It's just a bar graph that shows the past twelve months on there.
stewart_read: The bill amount was never captured (customer said he didn't know), and the rep never circles back to make the customer curious about his usage/savings — bill collection becomes a photo-later formality only.
coaching_implication: Even without a number, the rep could reflect the son's low bill mentioned earlier (03:32) back as a curiosity hook ("let's see if we can get you numbers like that") instead of leaving it flat.

quote: his house has got huge numbers of solar panels... his bill is very small. So why not?
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong peer-proof signal (son's low bill) and an unprompted "why not" — genuine buy-in language the rep does not reflect back or use later.
coaching_implication: This line is a ready-made anchor ("let's see if we can get your bill looking like your son's") that the rep should reuse when booking the appointment or handling the timing pushback.

quote: it's not gonna happen this week, probably even another because I've just got too many irons in the fire.
stewart_read: Customer gives a timing objection and the rep accepts it with zero counter-attempt — no alternative day offered, no firm callback time set.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be reading the caregiving context as a reason not to push, prioritizing goodwill over a hard close — but goodwill and a locked callback time are not mutually exclusive.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proposed a specific callback window (e.g., "how about I check back with you in two weeks once things calm down?") rather than leaving it fully open-ended.
